[needs-review-audit-2026-09-17]
Reviewed adapter: Pine · Overnight block.
Verdict: Retain NQ 15m; ES remains conditional and YM fails cost resilience.
NQ 15m / 17:00-06:00 New York is positive in all saved 2024-2026 baseline and doubled-cost checks. The 2026 baseline earns $71,380 with 26.10% drawdown and 172 trades; doubled costs leave $69,230. Both earlier entry-time neighbors are positive. The catalog already marks this configuration Working, but not feasible because event-order delay remains untested.
The NQ 2026 result retains $24,597.50 after arithmetically removing its five best trades, with profit factor 1.34. The 17:00 scheduling boundary normally fills at the 18:00 reopen; these are overnight positions by design.
ES 5m passes later numeric checks, but the 16:00 entry sensitivity loses $2,090 over 2022-2023. Its review flag is a timing-robustness issue, not failure of the displayed 2024 baseline. YM 15m earns only $2,337.50 in 2025 at base costs and loses $875 with doubled costs.
Next step: Validate NQ entry/exit latency and overnight risk at minute resolution. Resolve ES timing robustness with a separately declared test; keep YM out of a passing classification.
Audit: all 334 current-adapter runs reconciled; data/source/artifact checksums verified. No failed evidence removed and no automatic promotion.
Full review: reports/needs-review-2026-09-17/REVIEW.md#pine-overnight-block

input.criteria: Net return >= 0.000001; drawdown <= 0.2; trades >= 60 across test folds
input.hypothesis: Fixed five-minute NQ reversal candidate selected from already inspected timing research. Freeze decline 1.25%, SMA200, one-session long, no renewal, one flat session, five-minute entry tolerance, one contract and $100000. No further selection, sizing or threshold changes. Native six rolling 365-day test folds cover 2020-09-05 through 2026-09-03, with preceding 365-day training and one fixed candidate (minimum one training trade; selection metric net P&L). Every aggregated declared scenario must have positive net return, >=60 trades and <=20% minute-close drawdown. Native event evaluation supports baseline and doubled costs only, so mandatory supplemental continuous tests cover five-minute doubled costs and offsets four/six minutes at normal and doubled costs. All continuous cases, including the saved five-minute baseline, must satisfy the same gates. Four-minute offset is an earlier timing neighbor, six-minute offset models one-minute scheduling delay to both entry and exit. No generic event-order latency is claimed. Historical development validation only, not untouched holdout. Prior 09:30 campaign and daily-delay failures remain retained.

strategy.migration_scope: Same long-only daily signal as short-term-reversal v1.1 with trend filter, one-session hold and renewal disabled (one mandatory flat interval). Completed 09:30-16:00 New York RTH bars generate signals; partial current days never contribute. A completed minute at/after 09:30 plus the configured offset schedules a next-open fill. Late new entries are suppressed; entry orders expire after the lateness allowance, exit orders expire at that RTH close and are resubmitted at subsequent opening windows. Warmup never synthesizes a position. Full-trading-day minute marks include overnight but exclude 17:00-18:00 and weekends. Native warmup is undeclared because minute counts cannot prove daily initialization; the model separately requires sufficient completed pre-start RTH days. No authoritative holiday calendar, per-contract roll execution, intraminute stop/target, or margin model. Prior daily-shift failure remains unresolved; not an automatic status promotion.

The frozen NQ 5m / 2R rule passes saved numeric checks, but nine unique baseline trades cross the local entry date across 2024, 2025 and Jan-Aug 2026: two, five and two respectively. The audited carry P&L is $3,570, $162.50 and -$3,645. These are actual overnight exposures in a strategy intended to flatten intraday.
The adapter only issues a force-flat order when an observed bar falls in its flatten window; its next-opening safety action cannot retroactively close a missing-window trade. The earlier minute-data exit audit found no entry-day flatten-window quotes for the flagged holiday/short-session cases.
The app's preferred 2.5R run is a 2022-2023 sensitivity case, not the frozen 2R validation. It earns $52,727.50, but it also carries two trades overnight. Changing reward/risk does not fix the exit defect.
The 2025 and 2026 baseline results become negative after removing their five best trades. The 2026 baseline has only 29 trades.
Next step: Create a separate execution revision with an authoritative session calendar and explicit shortened-session/no-quote policy, then replay the frozen parameters. Preserve these original ledgers; do not claim the unchanged code is intraday-safe.
